experiment_name: POLICY_ONLY vs PUCT_4 ablation: does search add value over the bare policy head, 500-update checkpoint

algorithm_config.seat_rotation: 4 seats x 10 seeds = 40 games per policy

policies_compared.policy_only: legal mask + policy-head softmax (MonopolyZeroNet.predict) + legal argmax, no search
policies_compared.puct_4: MaxNPUCT, simulations=4, max_depth=16, self_play=False (the search config used by every prior MonopolyZero evaluation in this project)

algorithm_config.shadow_query_method: during puct_4's 40 games, policy_only is additionally asked what it would choose at every non-forced decision the checkpoint faces (same frozen pre-step state), without acting on it - the disagreement rate is measured on these exact decision states, not a separate offline sample

result: KILL the current PUCT/MCTS inference path. Both policies won exactly 2/40 held-out games (5.0%, identical Wilson-95 interval [1.4%, 16.5%]) on the same checkpoint/seeds/seats - PUCT_4 shows no statistically supported advantage over POLICY_ONLY (puct_4_improvement_over_policy_only_statistically_supported: false), and POLICY_ONLY shows no supported advantage over PUCT_4 either - they are indistinguishable within this sample. On the 31,535 non-forced decisions PUCT_4's own 40 evaluation games actually visited, POLICY_ONLY would have chosen the same action 97.07% of the time (2.93% disagreement) - a small fraction, consistent with 017's earlier finding that simulation-count scaling (4-vs-16) barely moves decisions on this checkpoint. PUCT_4 costs materially more per decision for that: p50 latency +8.6ms (0.0098s vs 0.0013s, ~7.7x), p95 +33.6ms (0.0384s vs 0.0048s, ~8.0x), for zero measurable win-rate benefit. Per the task's own decision rule: PUCT_4 shows no measurable/consistent advantage -> KILL search as currently used. POLICY_ONLY is equal (not worse) -> the next experiment should pivot toward a search-free learning objective/architecture rather than further MCTS tuning. No new training data or self-play games were generated; ASU was not imported (asu_modules_loaded: []); zero illegal actions/crashes in either policy across 80 games.
notes: integrity.fallbacks is the sum of both policies' fixed-agent fallback totals (151 policy_only-side games + 128 puct_4-side games = 279) - these are LocalFixedPolicy substitutions for the three non-focus opponent seats, not fallbacks by the checkpoint itself; the checkpoint (either policy) had 0 illegal actions in both runs. action_disagreement_states (31,535) counts every non-forced decision across puct_4's 40 games, not a fixed offline sample like 017's 200 states - the raw per-decision shadow-query list itself (record: turn_index/seat/actual_action/shadow_action/agree) was NOT persisted to raw_logs (would be several MB of small dicts); only the aggregate rate is recorded here, matching this project's small-raw-stdout convention. Despite the low disagreement rate, both policies happened to win on the exact same two (seed, seat) pairs (32001/seat1, 32009/seat1) - not a bug (verified: per-game decision counts differ slightly between the two policies on shared seeds, e.g. 6687 vs 5775 decisions on seed 32001/seat0, confirming genuinely different trajectories where they occurred) - this is the expected consequence of a ~97% agreement rate: most games play out nearly identically since the two policies mostly choose the same actions, so most outcomes coincide too.
